title: SpinalExpect_Invasive
description: This dataset investigates whether temporal expectation modulates initial sensory processing in the human spinal cord using invasive electrophysiological recordings. Eight patients with neuropathic pain and implanted cervical epidural electrodes performed an auditory-cued median nerve stimulation task under two conditions: fixed (1100 ms) or variable (100-2100 ms) cue-to-stimulus intervals. Participants counted rare double-stimulus trials (80 ms interstimulus interval) within ~5 minute blocks. The study examines how predictability of sensory input affects spinal cord processing mechanisms.
methods_description: Invasive electrophysiological recordings from eight epidural contacts (3 mm length, 1 mm spacing) placed alongside the dorsal cervical spinal cord in patients with cervical epidural electrode implantation. Electric median nerve stimulation was delivered at the left wrist, preceded by auditory cues. Experimental design alternated between fixed (1100 ms) and variable (100-2100 ms uniform distribution) cue-to-stimulus intervals across blocks.
